references.text: The angel's command to Hagar to name her son Ishmael, which means 'God hears'. Verse 15 shows that Abraham obeyed this message and gave his son this name.
Sarah sees Ishmael mocking, which leads her to ask Abraham to send away Hagar and Ishmael. This illustrates the consequences of Abraham's actions with Hagar.
This passage lists the descendants of Ishmael, showing the fulfillment of God's promise to make Ishmael into a great nation.
God promises to bless Ishmael and make him fruitful, with twelve princes as his descendants and to become a great people.
Paul uses the story of Hagar and Sarah as an allegory for the two covenants, where Hagar represents the old covenant.
Connects the event of Ishmael's birth and naming directly to the subsequent genealogy of his line.
Creates a theological contrast between the birth of Ishmael (human effort) and Isaac (divine promise).
Confirms Ishmael's status as Abraham's son in the overall genealogy, consistent with the event in Genesis 16:15.
Forms a narrative arc from the problem (barrenness in v. 1) to the solution (the birth of Ishmael in v. 15).
Describes the cause (v. 3) and effect (v. 15) in the sequence of events that led to Ishmael's birth.
Shows that Ishmael, born in 16:15, was included in God's covenant sign (circumcision) in 17:23.
Links Ishmael's birth to the formation of the 'Ishmaelites' as a distinct people in later times.
Creates a theological contrast between Sarah's miraculous birth and Hagar's natural birth.
